title: Perspectives and challenges in circularly polarized luminescence of lanthanide(III) complexes: From solution-based systems to solid-state applications
claim: Ligand-to-Ln energy transfer switches from short-range exchange to longer-range multipolar resonance: exchange needs orbital overlap and is effective below about 4 Å with ΔJ = 0, ±1, whereas dipole–dipole transfer falls as R^-6 and dominates beyond about 4 Å.
explanation: Exchange moves population from the ligand excited state to the Ln excited state while the Ln ground-state population returns to the ligand. Dipole–dipole transfer does not require overlap. Higher multipoles (dipole–quadrupole, quadrupole–quadrupole) fall off more steeply, stated as R^-8 and R^-10.
scope: Nonradiative ligand-to-Ln(III) sensitization in coordination compounds.
conditions: Exchange selection rule quoted as ΔJ = 0, ±1 (with J′ ≠ 0 in the review’s wording). Distance threshold about 4 Å.
caveats: The review’s sentence that efficiency “decreases as the Ln–ligand distances become short” is inconsistent with the stated <4 Å contribution and is treated as a wording error; the distance rule itself is taken from the accompanying mechanism description and ref. 68.
